content: Amoxicillin and clavulanic acid is a combination medication prescribed to treat bacterial infections, including those affecting the ears, lungs, sinuses, skin, and urinary tract. Amoxicillin belongs to the penicillin-like class of antibiotics and works by inhibiting bacterial growth. Clavulanic acid, a beta-lactamase inhibitor, prevents bacteria from breaking down amoxicillin, thereby enhancing its effectiveness. It is important to note that antibiotics, including this combination, are ineffective against viral infections such as colds or the flu. This medication is available in various forms, including tablets, chewable tablets, and liquid suspensions, and is taken orally. It is typically administered with a meal or snack either every 8 hours (three times daily) or every 12 hours (twice daily). To ensure consistent dosing, take the medication at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not alter the prescribed dosage or frequency. Shake the liquid suspension well before each use to ensure even distribution of the medication. Chewable tablets must be thoroughly chewed before swallowing, while other tablets should be taken with a full glass of water. Be aware that the 250 mg and 500 mg tablets contain the same amount of clavulanic acid, so two 250 mg tablets should not be substituted for one 500 mg tablet. Additionally, the 250 mg regular tablet and the 250 mg chewable tablet contain different amounts of clavulanic acid and should not be interchanged. Complete the full course of the medication, even if you feel better, as stopping prematurely may lead to bacterial resistance. Amoxicillin and clavulanic acid may also be used to treat certain sexually transmitted diseases (STDs). Discuss the potential risks and benefits of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. It may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to amoxicillin, clavulanic acid, penicillin, cephalosporins, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially allopurinol or probenecid, as dose adjustments or monitoring may be necessary. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, allergies, asthma, hay fever, hives, or mononucleosis. Be aware that this medication may reduce the effectiveness of oral contraceptives (birth control pills), so consider using an alternative form of birth control while taking it. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Minor side effects include diarrhea, upset stomach, vomiting, and mild skin rash. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects requiring immediate medical attention include severe skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, vaginal itching and discharge, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Tablets should be stored at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Liquid medication should be refrigerated, tightly closed, and discarded after 10 days. Do not freeze the liquid form. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly; consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include stomach pain, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, hyperactivity, and drowsiness. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests may be ordered to monitor your response to the medication. If you have diabetes, use Clinistix or TesTape (not Clinitest) to test your urine for sugar while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If symptoms of infection persist after completing the medication, contact your doctor.
